stem: A tutoring center charges a one-time registration fee of \$35 plus \$18 per lesson. Marcus wants to spend at most \$250 at the center. The inequality \(35 + 18n \le 250\) represents this situation, where \(n\) is the number of lessons. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the solution set of this inequality?

choices.A: Marcus can afford at most 11 lessons.
choices.B: Marcus can afford at most 12 lessons.
choices.C: Each lesson costs Marcus at most \$11.90.
choices.D: Marcus must take at least 11 lessons.

solution: The number of lessons is a whole number, so the greatest number Marcus can afford is 11.
Check: 11 lessons cost \(35 + 198 = 233\) dollars; 12 lessons cost \(251\) dollars, which is over the limit.

explanation.A: Correct. \(n \le 11.94\), and since lessons are whole, Marcus can afford at most 11 lessons.
explanation.B: Incorrect. 12 lessons would cost \(35 + 18(12) = 251\) dollars, which is more than \$250. The decimal 11.94 must be rounded down, not up.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The solution set describes the number of lessons; the cost per lesson is the fixed \$18.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The inequality is \(\le\), a limit on spending; it gives a maximum number of lessons, not a minimum.

verify:
n = symbols('n')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(35 + 18*n <= 250, n, relational=False)
assert floor(s.sup) == 11 and s.sup < 12
assert 'at most 11 lessons' in choices[answer]
assert all('at most 11 lessons' not in choices[k] for k in choices if k != answer)
